basu-low-pe-1977.title: Low Price-Earnings Portfolios
basu-low-pe-1977.lede: Rank stocks by price relative to reported earnings and favor the lowest P/E group. This is a direct earnings-yield value screen rather than a forecast of earnings growth.

bernard-thomas-1989.title: Inspired by Bernard and Thomas: Post-Earnings Drift (SUE)
bernard-thomas-1989.lede: Stocks keep drifting in the direction of a quarterly earnings surprise for about 60 trading days. Bernard and Thomas (1990) trace it to prices acting as if earnings follow a seasonal random walk, ignoring their autocorrelation.

bollinger-band-squeeze-breakout.title: Inspired by Bollinger: Band Squeeze and Breakout
bollinger-band-squeeze-breakout.lede: Bands placed around a moving average scale price dispersion by recent volatility. A contraction in band width can flag a low-volatility regime before a directional move, but the bands alone do not determine direction.

buffett-owner-earnings.title: Inspired by Buffett: Moats and Owner Earnings
buffett-owner-earnings.lede: Buy businesses with durable competitive advantages at sensible prices, valued on owner earnings (true distributable cash), and hold.

carhart-1997.title: Inspired by Carhart: Momentum as a Fourth Factor
carhart-1997.lede: Adding a one-year momentum factor to the Fama-French three factors, together with fund expenses and trading costs, almost completely explains persistence in mutual fund returns.

carlisle-acquirers-2014.title: Inspired by Carlisle: The Acquirer's Multiple
carlisle-acquirers-2014.lede: Carlisle argues cheapness alone (EV / operating earnings) beats the Magic Formula because high returns on capital tend to mean-revert, so the quality rank adds little.

chan-jegadeesh-lakonishok-earnings-momen.title: Earnings-Surprise Momentum
chan-jegadeesh-lakonishok-earnings-momen.lede: Both prior price performance and prior earnings news predict subsequent returns. Sorting on earnings surprises provides a momentum signal distinct from price-only momentum.

connors-rsi2-2008.title: Inspired by Connors and Alvarez: RSI(2) Mean Reversion
connors-rsi2-2008.lede: In uptrending markets, deep short-term oversold readings (2-period RSI) mark high-probability bounce entries.

cooper-asset-growth-2008.title: Asset Growth Anomaly
cooper-asset-growth-2008.lede: Firms that grow total assets fastest earn lower later returns than slow growers and shrinkers. The authors lean toward investors overextrapolating growth.

darvas-box-1960.title: Inspired by Darvas: The Darvas Box
darvas-box-1960.lede: Stocks move in stacked 'boxes'; buy the break of the box ceiling at new highs with a stop just below it.

dreman-contrarian-low-pe-1980.title: Inspired by Dreman: Contrarian Low-P/E
dreman-contrarian-low-pe-1980.lede: Buy companies that the market values at depressed multiples, especially low P/E, while avoiding a fashionable consensus-growth approach. The approach is explicitly contrarian and emphasizes diversification.

external-financing-anomaly.title: Inspired by Bradshaw, Richardson and Sloan: External Financing
external-financing-anomaly.lede: Net cash raised from outside investors can signal weak future profitability or overly optimistic valuation. Aggregating debt and equity financing avoids treating one funding channel in isolation.

fama-french-1992.title: Inspired by Fama and French: Value Factor (HML)
fama-french-1992.lede: High book-to-market stocks earn a premium over low book-to-market stocks not explained by beta.

george-hwang-2004.title: Inspired by George and Hwang: 52-Week High Momentum
george-hwang-2004.lede: Nearness to the 52-week high forecasts returns better than past returns, and its gains do not reverse later; the authors attribute this to investors anchoring on the 52-week high when judging news.

graham-defensive-1949.title: Inspired by Graham: Defensive Investor Screen
graham-defensive-1949.lede: A mechanical quality-value checklist protects the amateur: size, financial strength, earnings stability, dividends, and a sane price.

gray-carlisle-quantitative-value-2012.title: Inspired by Gray and Carlisle: Quantitative Value
gray-carlisle-quantitative-value-2012.lede: Screen out likely manipulators and distressed firms, buy the cheapest stocks on EBIT / enterprise value, then keep the highest quality. The book tests many value ratios and picks EBIT/EV as the best single measure.

greenblatt-magic-2005.title: Inspired by Greenblatt: Magic Formula
greenblatt-magic-2005.lede: Rank the market on cheapness (earnings yield) plus quality (return on capital); buy the best combined ranks mechanically.

jegadeesh-titman-1993.title: Inspired by Jegadeesh and Titman: Cross-Sectional Momentum
jegadeesh-titman-1993.lede: Stocks that outperformed over the past 3-12 months keep outperforming over the next 3-12 months.

johnson-so-option-stock-volume.title: Inspired by Johnson and So: Option-to-Stock Volume
johnson-so-option-stock-volume.lede: Unusually heavy options trading relative to underlying-share trading can reveal negative private information when stock shorting is costly. The signal does not require classifying option trades as buys or sells.

livermore-pivotal-1940.title: Inspired by Livermore: Pivotal Points
livermore-pivotal-1940.lede: Wait for the pivotal point - the price where the line of least resistance breaks - and pyramid only into profit.

lo-mackinlay-1990.title: Inspired by Jegadeesh and Lehmann: Short-Horizon Reversal
lo-mackinlay-1990.lede: At the 1-week to 1-month horizon, returns reverse: last period's losers beat last period's winners. Later work links the effect to liquidity provision.

low-vol-anomaly.title: Low-Volatility Anomaly
low-vol-anomaly.lede: Low-volatility and low-beta US stocks have earned similar or higher returns than high-volatility stocks with much less risk, the opposite of what the CAPM predicts.

lsv-1994.title: Inspired by Lakonishok, Shleifer and Vishny: Contrarian Value
lsv-1994.lede: Value works because investors extrapolate past growth too far: low-priced, slow-growth stocks beat glamour stocks, and the gap is not explained by higher risk.

minervini-sepa-2013.title: Minervini Trend Template (SEPA)
minervini-sepa-2013.lede: Superperformance stocks are in confirmed stage-2 uptrends before their biggest gains; an eight-point template filters for them.

neff-lowpe-1999.title: Neff's Low-P/E + Yield Discipline
neff-lowpe-1999.lede: Buy solid growers at low P/Es with dividends; the 'total return / P/E' ratio finds them.

novy-marx-2013.title: Gross Profitability
novy-marx-2013.lede: Gross profits / assets predicts returns about as well as book-to-market. Profitable firms earn more despite higher valuations, so the strategy is a growth tilt that hedges value.

novy-marx-profitable-value-2013.title: Inspired by Novy-Marx: Profitable Value
novy-marx-profitable-value-2013.lede: Combine a conventional value screen with gross profitability, because profitable firms can be attractive even when their book-to-market alone does not identify them. The combination avoids treating all cheap firms as equivalent.

oneil-canslim-1988.title: Inspired by O'Neil: CANSLIM
oneil-canslim-1988.lede: Growth leaders share seven traits before big runs: current and annual earnings acceleration, new highs/products, tight supply, leadership, institutional sponsorship, and a confirmed market.

oneil-cup-handle.title: Inspired by O'Neil: Cup-with-Handle Breakout
oneil-cup-handle.lede: Winners consolidate in a rounded 'cup' with a shallow 'handle', then break out on volume - the entry point of the CANSLIM system.

oshaughnessy-1996.title: Inspired by O'Shaughnessy: What Works on Wall Street
oshaughnessy-1996.lede: Decades of factor tests distilled: combined value composites (P/S, P/E, EV/EBITDA, P/CF, yield) beat any single ratio.

piotroski-2000.title: Piotroski F-Score
piotroski-2000.lede: Within cheap (high B/M) stocks, nine simple accounting signals separate the recovering from the dying.

qmj-2019.title: Inspired by Asness, Frazzini and Pedersen: Quality Minus Junk
qmj-2019.lede: Safe, profitable, growing firms trade at only modestly higher prices than junk, so long quality, short junk earned positive risk-adjusted returns.

roic-persistence.title: Inspired by Practitioners: ROIC Persistence and Compounders
roic-persistence.lede: Businesses that earn high returns on invested capital and can reinvest at those returns compound value. The bet is that returns fade more slowly than the price implies; data show ROIC does revert toward the mean.

schloss-approach.title: Inspired by Schloss: Cheap-Asset Basket
schloss-approach.lede: Buy many statistically cheap stocks trading below book value and near multi-year lows, with little debt; rely on the balance sheet, not the story.

shareholder-yield-2005.title: Inspired by Priest and Faber: Shareholder Yield
shareholder-yield-2005.lede: Dividends plus net buybacks (and, in Priest's version, net debt paydown) measure cash returned to holders better than dividends alone.

sloan-1996.title: Accruals Anomaly
sloan-1996.lede: Earnings driven by accruals persist less than earnings backed by cash, but prices act as if investors weight both the same, so high-accrual firms later disappoint.

stattman-book-to-market-1980.title: High Book-to-Market Stocks
stattman-book-to-market-1980.lede: Use book equity relative to market capitalization to identify stocks priced cheaply relative to accounting net worth. Hold the higher book-to-market stocks rather than the lower book-to-market stocks.

turtle-donchian-1983.title: Inspired by Dennis and Eckhardt: Turtle Breakout
turtle-donchian-1983.lede: Trend following is teachable: buy 20/55-day channel breakouts with volatility-sized positions and hard exit rules.

weinstein-stages-1988.title: Inspired by Weinstein: Stage Analysis
weinstein-stages-1988.lede: Every stock cycles through four stages; buy Stage 2 breakouts above a rising 30-week MA, sell in Stage 3 and short Stage 4 breakdowns.
